meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There's a lot of blood, sweat and guts between dreams and success'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Bear Bryant everywhere, sourced nowhere. Here is exactly how thin the paper trail is.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: The line is credited to Bryant almost everywhere it appears, and it sounds like him. But we could not find a contemporary printing: the only citation Wikiquote gives is a 2012 blog post listing fifty Bryant quotes, which is a repetition rather than a source.

source.heading: A quote with no paper trail

docMeta.dd: A 2012 online list of Bryant quotations

source.excerpt: There's a lot of blood, sweat and guts between dreams and success.
trail: Wikiquote’s Bear Bryant page ↗ lists the line in its main Quotes section, but the only citation attached is a 2012 post on a college-football blog titled “Top Fifty Quotes From Bear Bryant” — a compilation, not a record of him saying it.
Quote Investigator ↗ has traced exactly one Bryant saying, and it is not this one, so no specialist has established a first appearance.

We searched the Library of Congress’s Chronicling America newspaper corpus for “blood, sweat and guts” and for “between dreams and success” and found no match. That corpus thins out sharply after the early 1960s, so this is weak evidence of absence rather than proof — we note it as a search we ran, not as a verdict.
Bryant’s own autobiography, Bear ↗, is catalogued at the Internet Archive as a 1975 Little, Brown printing, but it is lending-restricted, so we could not search it for the line.
source.excerptNote: We have no earlier or fuller context to offer, because we could not find an appearance of the line in Bryant’s lifetime. That absence is the honest finding here.
source.rightsNote: Because we could not identify where or when this wording first appeared, we make no claim about its copyright status. If it was first printed in Bryant’s lifetime it would almost certainly be in copyright; we simply do not know, and would rather say so than guess.

author.name: Bear Bryant
author.heading: About Bear Bryant
author.bio: Paul William “Bear” Bryant coached the Alabama Crimson Tide from 1958 to 1982, winning six national championships and thirteen conference titles, and retired holding the record for the most wins of any coach in college football history. He got the nickname as a teenager for agreeing to wrestle a carnival bear. He is one of the most quoted figures in American sport and one of the least well documented.

misattribution.heading: Credited everywhere, sourced nowhere
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is claiming this line, and nothing suggests Bryant did not say it. What is missing is any record of him saying it.

items.why: The citation Wikiquote ↗ attaches is a 2012 web post collecting fifty Bryant quotations. A list of quotes repeats an attribution; it does not document one.
Quote Investigator ↗ has published on only one Bryant saying — the “size of the dog in the fight” line — and has not looked at this one.

misattribution.truthLine: Treat it as attributed rather than documented: entirely plausible, thoroughly repeated, and so far unsupported by any source printed while Bryant was alive.

context.heading: Why an undocumented quote still matters
lead: Bryant won six national championships at Alabama and retired in 1982 holding the record for most wins by a college football coach, so a maxim about grinding toward a goal fits him about as well as a quote can fit anyone. That plausibility is exactly what lets an unsourced line travel.
It is a useful reminder that “sounds like him” is not evidence. Most famous coach quotations reach us through motivational posters rather than transcripts, and the posters do not keep receipts.
